blocks.x: Berth productivity +16%, planning platform and crane health sensing

A container-terminal operator: Logistics operations lose money in the gaps: idle fleets, dwell time and manual re-planning. The Achala program started with the route economics —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.
Berth planning static vs. yard reality; anchorage waits cost.
Cranes failed unscheduled; throughput lost. Ransomware exposure post-industry incidents; recovery untested.

The planning platform unified vessel/yard/tide data with scenario engines; crane telemetry drives predictive maintenance; a Quanta tournament on stowage formulations delivered 5% handling-time gains (industrialized); and IT/OT segmentation plus restore-tested recovery proved restart at 6 hours in drills.
